title: Ezekiel Chapter 27 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 27 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 27 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 27.

questions.question: What did the LORD instruct Ezekiel to take up for Tyrus?
questions.explanation: The LORD instructed Ezekiel to take up a lamentation for Tyrus in Ezekiel 27:2.

questions.question: Which city is described as being at the entry of the sea and a merchant of the people?
questions.explanation: The city described as being at the entry of the sea and a merchant is Tyrus (Tyre) in Ezekiel 27:3.

questions.question: What materials were used to make the ship boards for Tyrus?
questions.explanation: The ship boards of Tyrus were made of fir trees of Senir as stated in Ezekiel 27:5.

questions.question: True or False: The wise men of Gebal were calkers for Tyrus.
questions.explanation: The wise men of Gebal were indeed calkers for Tyrus, as mentioned in Ezekiel 27:9.

questions.question: Who were the mariners of Tyrus?
questions.explanation: The inhabitants of Zidon and Arvad were specifically mentioned as the mariners of Tyrus in Ezekiel 27:8.

questions.question: Which materials did Tarshish trade in Tyrus's fairs?
questions.explanation: Tarshish traded silver, iron, tin, and lead in Tyrus's fairs according to Ezekiel 27:12.

questions.question: True or False: The company of Ashurites made benches of cedar for Tyrus.
questions.explanation: The company of Ashurites made benches of ivory, not cedar, as stated in Ezekiel 27:6.

questions.question: Which materials were used for the sails of Tyrus?
options: Fine linen with broidered work from Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: Fine linen with broidered work from Egypt
questions.explanation: The sails of Tyrus were made of fine linen with broidered work from Egypt as mentioned in Ezekiel 27:7.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 27:10 mention about the people of Persia, Lud, and Phut?
options: They were part of Tyrus's army
questions.correctAnswer: They were part of Tyrus's army
questions.explanation: The verse states that they were in Tyrus's army, specifically mentioned in Ezekiel 27:10.

questions.question: True or False: The men of Arvad were responsible for building Tyrus's towers.
questions.explanation: The Gammadims were in Tyrus's towers, not the men of Arvad, as stated in Ezekiel 27:11.

questions.question: What kind of clothing did Dedan provide for Tyrus?
questions.explanation: Dedan was a merchant of precious clothes for chariots as stated in Ezekiel 27:20.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 27 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 27 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who were the merchants that traded the persons of men and vessels of brass in Tyrus' market?
questions.explanation: Javan, Tubal, and Meshech are specifically mentioned as merchants trading persons and vessels of brass in Ezekiel 27:13.

questions.question: What items did the house of Togarmah trade in Tyrus' fairs?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:14 states that the house of Togarmah traded in horses, horsemen, and mules.

questions.question: True or False: The merchants of Sheba and Raamah traded in precious stones and gold.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:22 confirms that the merchants of Sheba and Raamah occupied in Tyrus' fairs with spices, precious stones, and gold.

questions.question: Which city was mentioned as a merchant for the multitude of wares made by Tyrus?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:18 indicates that Damascus was a merchant in the multitude of wares of Tyrus.

questions.question: What was traded in the fairs of Tyrus by Syria?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:16 describes Syria's merchants occupying in Tyrus' fairs with emeralds, purple, and broidered work.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 27:20 say Dedan traded?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:20 clearly states that Dedan was a merchant in precious clothes for chariots.

questions.question: True or False: The men of Dedan were known for trading in livestock.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:15 mentions that the men of Dedan traded with horns of ivory and ebony, not livestock.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 27:33 highlight the impact Tyrus had on other nations?
options: It enriched the kings of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: It enriched the kings of the earth
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:33 states that Tyrus filled many people and enriched the kings of the earth with its merchandise.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 27:19 say Dan and Javan traded in?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:19 specifies that Dan and Javan traded bright iron, cassia, and calamus in Tyrus' fairs.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 27 teach about the consequences of Tyrus' downfall?
options: It will bring wealth to other nations
It will cause fear and astonishment
questions.correctAnswer: It will cause fear and astonishment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:35 states that the inhabitants of the isles and their kings shall be astonished and afraid at Tyrus' ruin.

questions.question: True or False: The merchants of Tyrus included the princes of Kedar.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:21 confirms that Arabia and the princes of Kedar occupied with Tyrus as merchants.

questions.question: Which materials were traded in Tyrus' fairs according to Ezekiel 27:24?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:24 lists blue clothes, broidered work, and chests of rich apparel as items among Tyrus' merchandise.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 27:27 predict will happen to Tyrus' merchandise?
options: It will fall into the seas
It will be taken by other nations
It will be stored for future use
questions.correctAnswer: It will fall into the seas
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:27 states that all of Tyrus' riches and company shall fall into the seas in the day of their ruin.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 27 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 27.

questions.question: What was said about the merchants of Tarshish in Ezekiel 27:25?
options: They sang of Tyrus in the market
They were the pilots of the sea
questions.correctAnswer: They sang of Tyrus in the market
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:25 states, 'The ships of Tarshish did sing of thee in thy market: and thou wast replenished, and made very glorious in the midst of the seas.' This highlights the prosperity and glory of Tyrus.

questions.question: What consequence does Tyrus face according to Ezekiel 27:27?
options: Its riches and company will fall into the seas
It will become a great nation
It will be praised by all merchants
questions.correctAnswer: Its riches and company will fall into the seas
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:27 indicates that 'Thy riches, and thy fairs, thy merchandise...shall fall into the midst of the seas in the day of thy ruin,' showing the impending judgment on Tyrus.

questions.question: Who will express their grief for Tyrus as stated in Ezekiel 27:31?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:31 mentions that 'they shall weep for thee with bitterness of heart and bitter wailing,' indicating the widespread mourning for Tyrus’s downfall.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 27:30, what actions will the mariners take upon witnessing the fall of Tyrus?
options: They will cast up dust upon their heads
questions.correctAnswer: They will cast up dust upon their heads
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:30 states, 'they shall cast up dust upon their heads,' which is a sign of mourning and despair in the ancient Near Eastern culture.

questions.question: What metaphor is used in Ezekiel 27:26 to describe the destruction of Tyrus?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:26 mentions, 'the east wind hath broken thee in the midst of the seas,' symbolizing the swift and destructive nature of Tyrus's ruin.

questions.question: Which group is noted as the lamenters in Ezekiel 27:32?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:32 states they shall take up a lamentation for Tyrus, showing that even those who benefited from Tyrus's trade mourn its destruction.

questions.question: True or False: The inhabitants of the isles will be astonished at Tyrus according to Ezekiel 27:35.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:35 states, 'All the inhabitants of the isles shall be astonished at thee,' indicating that Tyrus's fall would have a significant impact on neighboring regions.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 27:34 say will happen to Tyrus in the depths of the waters?
options: Its riches and company shall fall
questions.correctAnswer: Its riches and company shall fall
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:34 states, 'thy merchandise and all thy company in the midst of thee shall fall,' emphasizing the total collapse of Tyrus's economic and social structure.

questions.question: What historical city is often compared to Tyrus in its downfall?
questions.explanation: The downfall of Tyrus is often paralleled with that of Babylon, both cities representing pride and eventual judgment, as seen in Isaiah 47:1-15.

questions.question: What key term referring to a merchant's role in the economy is discussed in Ezekiel 27:13?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:13 describes 'Javan, Tubal, and Meshech, they were thy merchants,' emphasizing the vital role of merchants in Tyrus's economy.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 27:36 depicts Tyrus as a terror to merchants among the people.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:36 states, 'thou shalt be a terror,' indicating the fear and dread associated with Tyrus's fall among other merchants.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Ezekiel 27 to describe Tyrus's downfall?
questions.explanation: The chapter uses metaphorical language, such as comparing Tyrus to a ship that will sink, to illustrate its inevitable destruction.

questions.question: What does the term 'calakers' refer to in Ezekiel 27:27?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:27 includes 'thy calkers,' referring to those who would seal the ships, highlighting the skilled labor that contributed to Tyrus's maritime power.

questions.question: Which biblical book parallels the theme of economic judgment found in Ezekiel 27?
questions.explanation: Revelation 18 parallels Ezekiel 27's theme of judgment against a great commercial city, depicting the fall of Babylon in a similar manner.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 27 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 27 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 27 reveal about the pride of Tyrus?
options: Tyrus was humble before the Lord
Tyrus believed it was of perfect beauty
Tyrus was a city of destruction
questions.correctAnswer: Tyrus believed it was of perfect beauty
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:3 states that Tyrus said, 'I am of perfect beauty', highlighting its pride and self-sufficiency.

questions.question: Which materials were used to make Tyrus's ship boards according to Ezekiel 27?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:5 mentions that 'thy builders have perfected thy beauty' using 'ship boards of fir trees of Senir'.

questions.question: What does the presence of the wise men of Gebal in Tyrus suggest about the city's status?
options: Tyrus had a reputation for wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Tyrus had a reputation for wisdom
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:9 indicates that the wise men of Gebal were among Tyrus's calkers, suggesting Tyrus's status as a center of trade and knowledge.

questions.question: Which nations are mentioned as merchants in Tyrus’s trade?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:10 states that 'they of Persia and of Lud and of Phut were in thine army', indicating their involvement in Tyrus's trade.

questions.question: What did the merchants of Dedan trade with Tyrus?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:20 specifies that 'Dedan was thy merchant in precious clothes for chariots', indicating their specific trade.

questions.question: What specific attribute of God is revealed in His judgment on Tyrus?
questions.explanation: The judgment on Tyrus, as detailed throughout Ezekiel 27, reveals God's justice in dealing with pride and sin.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 27 connect to the broader redemptive narrative of Scripture?
options: It shows God's wrath against His people
It illustrates the fall of the proud and the restoration of the humble
It emphasizes the prosperity of the wicked
It highlights the futility of human wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates the fall of the proud and the restoration of the humble
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27 depicts the fall of Tyrus, symbolizing the ultimate downfall of pride and the hope for restoration for the humble, aligning with themes in James 4:6.

questions.question: What lamentation is taken up regarding Tyrus in Ezekiel 27?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:32 describes the lamentation taken up for Tyrus, lamenting its destruction and beauty, emphasizing the sadness of its fall.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 27 indicate about the fate of Tyrus's merchandise?
options: It will be shared among the nations
It will bring joy to the people
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:34 prophesies that 'thy merchandise and all thy company in the midst of thee shall fall', indicating imminent destruction.

questions.question: What specific lamentation do the merchants express in response to Tyrus's downfall?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:35 explains that 'all the inhabitants of the isles shall be astonished at thee', showing the impact of Tyrus's fall on its merchants.

questions.question: Which type of trade is highlighted in Ezekiel 27:13?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:13 notes that Javan, Tubal, and Meshech traded the 'persons of men', indicating a grim aspect of commerce in Tyrus.

questions.question: What does the imagery of Tyrus's ships singing in the market signify?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27:25 describes the ships of Tarshish singing of Tyrus in its market, symbolizing the joy and glory of its prosperous trade.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 27 reveal about the consequences of pride in Tyrus?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27 portrays the eventual downfall of Tyrus as a consequence of its pride, especially evident in verses describing its destruction.

questions.question: What is the significance of the various nations trading with Tyrus?
options: It demonstrates its lack of resources
questions.explanation: The diverse nations trading with Tyrus, as listed in Ezekiel 27, illustrate its significant influence and position as a trade hub in the ancient world.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 27 teach about the nature of God's judgment?
options: It is based on human standards
It is inevitable for the proud
questions.correctAnswer: It is inevitable for the proud
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 27 illustrates that God's judgment is inevitable for those who, like Tyrus, are prideful and disregard His sovereignty.
